name: Gig Economy
description: The procedural contract generator that gives a driver a reason to start the engine: courier runs, race challenges, getaway jobs. It owns offer generation — payout scaled by distance, risk, and the driver's tier — plus acceptance windows and completion payout, which is disbursed through economy.currency so every earning stays in the audited ledger. Contracts are expressed as quests in progression.quest_log rather than through a parallel objective system, deliberately: the quest UI, waypoints, and reward plumbing already exist, and a gig that did not appear in the quest log would feel like a scam. world locations for pickup and drop-off are read from the world graph (the point-of-interest network when one is present), but this component does not own the map. It also does not own which gigs are offered — tier gating belongs to social.street_rep_tiers — and it does not own the driving; a timed courier run is hard because of the route, not because of any trick here.

inputs.name: maxActiveGigs
inputs.description: Concurrent contracts a driver may hold. Low enough that accepting a gig is a commitment with an opportunity cost, not a collect-them-all.

inputs.name: offerRefreshSeconds
inputs.description: How often the offer board rotates. Rotation pressure is what makes a juicy contract feel found rather than waited for.

inputs.name: payoutPerKm
inputs.description: Base distance rate before risk and tier multipliers. Anchors the whole economy — tune this first, then the multipliers.

inputs.name: riskMultiplierCap
inputs.description: Ceiling on the risk multiplier for getaway and timed jobs. A cap keeps one lucky run from retiring the early game economy.

outputs.name: availableOffers
outputs.description: Current offer board. Read directly by the job-board UI; expires entries drop out on the refresh tick.

outputs.name: lifetimeGigEarnings
outputs.description: Total paid out across completed gigs, for stats screens and rep-tier context.
